inception2_19.speaker: director

inception2_20.dialogue: You are the quickest to learn anything new. The solution to any mystery is within your capabilities!

inception2_21.dialogue: We know about your achievements, Steve!

inception2_22.dialogue: All the operations you participated in were done excellently!

inception2_23.dialogue: I personally called you into my office,

inception2_24.dialogue: because you are the only one I can entrust such an important mission to.

inception2_25.dialogue: The fate of the entire planet is at stake!

inception2_27.dialogue: I will try to figure everything out. I won’t let you down, sir!

inception2_28.dialogue: Always stay one step ahead of your enemies...
inception2_28.speaker: director

inception2_29.dialogue: One mistake could destroy everything we've worked so long to build.

inception2_30.dialogue: The car that will take you to the mansion is waiting at the entrance.

inception2_34.dialogue: There are traps all over this abandoned mansion, and they are life-threatening.

inception2_35.dialogue: To disarm them, you need to enter the correct code.

inception2_36.dialogue: I believe in you. Call me anytime. Good luck!

inception3_01.speaker: anonymous
inception3_01.dialogue: Stop! Who goes there?! Halt, living creature!

inception3_02.dialogue: You are wandering here in vain! Such creatures are not allowed here!

inception3_04.dialogue: A weapon! It has a weapon!

inception3_05.dialogue: I’m calling the police, there are bandits here, help!

inception3_06.speaker: steve

inception3_07.speaker: robot
inception3_07.dialogue: Oh, hello, Agent Steve Harrison. Please put down the weapon.

inception3_08.dialogue: I just assumed it was looters, thought they were trying to break the door again. No one can enter the correct code.

inception3_10.dialogue: I’m just a third-generation robot, model R3.

inception3_11.dialogue: I’m not allowed to let any living being in here because no one knows about the deadly traps.

inception3_12.dialogue: Why are you here, Agent Harrison?

inception3_14.dialogue: So you’re a robot model R3, a robot assistant to humans.

inception3_15.dialogue: You strictly follow the three laws.

inception3_16.dialogue: Your duty is to listen to and help any human. Right?

inception3_18.dialogue: A robot cannot harm a human or, through inaction, allow a human to come to harm.

inception3_19.dialogue: A robot must obey the orders of a human, except where such orders would conflict with the First Law.

inception3_20.speaker: steve
inception3_20.dialogue: Great, then you’ll help me. Listen carefully!

inception3_21.dialogue: Kevin Mitnick created a virus capable of erasing all data from a computer’s memory and disrupting the global network. And he has already launched it.

inception3_23.dialogue: We have less than 18 hours to create an antivirus in Prolog.

inception3_24.dialogue: Will you help me study it?

inception3_25.speaker: robot
inception3_25.dialogue: Yes, that function is programmed into me.

inception3_26.dialogue: But you should know that in order to study Prolog, you need to step away from traditional forms of programming.

inception3_28.dialogue: Try to understand the logic of the language itself. Believe me, it's a quite beautiful and logical language.

inception3_29.dialogue: Very soon, you'll appreciate all its beauty and possibilities.

inception3_30.speaker: steve
inception3_30.dialogue: I have no doubt about that. Shall we move on to the lesson?

inception3_31.speaker: robot
inception3_31.dialogue: Let's get started! I have a tablet, which will help you learn more about the Prolog language. It can assist you with completing tasks.

inception3_32.speaker: steve
inception3_32.dialogue: Can I start with the theory?

inception4_start.speaker: robot
inception4_start.dialogue: A program in Prolog consists of a number of statements. Each of them can be one of three types: it can either be a fact, a rule, or a query.

inception4_01.dialogue: A fact is a phrase without conditions, a statement that a certain relationship holds.

inception4_02.speaker: steve
inception4_02.dialogue: Each fact must end with a period. For example: `likes('Steve', work).`

inception4_03.dialogue: A rule is a fact whose truth depends on the truth of other facts. It consists of a head and a body, separated by `:-` — the 'if' operator, an implication.

inception4_04.dialogue: The head of the rule is a predicate, and the body of the rule is a sequence of predicates separated by commas.

inception4_05.speaker: steve
inception4_05.dialogue:
A rule must end with a period.
For example: `likes(steve, X) :- likes(robot, X)`.

inception4_06.dialogue: A query is a sequence of predicates, separated by commas or semicolons, and ending with a period.

inception4_07.dialogue: A comma `,` corresponds to the conjunction 'and', and in mathematical logic, it denotes conjunction.

inception4_08.dialogue: A semicolon `;` corresponds to the conjunction 'or' and denotes disjunction. The predicate of a query is called the goal.

inception4_09.speaker: steve
inception4_09.dialogue: Got it, got it, I'll solve it right now!

inception4_10.speaker: robot
inception4_10.dialogue: Be careful. Make too many mistakes — and you won’t be able to continue.

inception4_failTask0_02.dialogue: Be careful, please. And keep an eye on your health. It seems you’re starting to get nervous...

inception4_failTask0_03.dialogue: Focus, agent! This is your last chance...

inception4_13.dialogue: ...Alright. I see it’s time to continue our journey... and our learning.

elaboration1_start.speaker: steve
elaboration1_start.dialogue: The first task has been successfully completed! I didn’t expect to finish it so quickly!

elaboration1_02.dialogue: I must admit, you are very smart and perceptive! I’m really happy for you!
elaboration1_02.speaker: robot

elaboration1_03.dialogue: A call came in from the director. I’m listening, sir!
elaboration1_03.speaker: steve

elaboration1_04.dialogue: Special Agent Steve Harrison, this is the Director of the FBI. I have urgent news for you!
elaboration1_04.speaker: director

elaboration1_05.dialogue: We’ve tracked Kevin Mitnick's location. He is somewhere in the house. Be careful! He may be armed!

elaboration1_06.dialogue: Got it. Any new information about Sarah Parker?
elaboration1_06.speaker: steve

elaboration1_07.dialogue: We’ve interviewed all the individuals involved in the case, but it didn’t yield any new information. No one saw or heard anything. It’s like she vanished into thin air.
elaboration1_07.speaker: director

elaboration1_08.dialogue: It feels like Mitnick is holding her somewhere close by...
elaboration1_08.speaker: steve

elaboration1_09.dialogue: This version also needs to be worked out. Good luck! You have an important mission ahead!
elaboration1_09.speaker: director

elaboration1_10.dialogue: It’s so dark and gloomy here! But there’s no time to waste. If Mitnick is somewhere in the house, Sarah should be nearby. Let’s head upstairs!
elaboration1_10.speaker: steve

elaboration1_11.dialogue: Be careful going up, sir! Some of the stairs have hidden traps. These are the next tasks...
elaboration1_11.speaker: robot

elaboration1_12.dialogue: I’ll take a look at the theory now.
elaboration1_12.speaker: robot

elaboration1_13.dialogue: The arguments of Prolog program statements are called terms, and the Prolog program itself can be seen as a network of relationships between terms.
elaboration1_13.speaker: steve

elaboration1_14.dialogue: Each term represents an object from the domain and is written as a sequence of letters from these categories: uppercase and lowercase letters, digits, and special characters.

elaboration1_15.dialogue: The main data objects are usually divided into three types of terms: constants, variables (simple terms), and structures (compound terms).

elaboration1_16.dialogue: A constant is a named specific object or specific relationship. For example: `steve`.

elaboration1_17.dialogue: A variable is an object whose value changes during the execution of the program. A variable name starts with an uppercase letter or an underscore. For example: `Who`, `_who`.

elaboration1_18.dialogue: A variable is called bound if there is an object it represents. If no such object exists, the variable is called free.

elaboration1_19.dialogue: A structure is an object consisting of a set of components — other objects. For example: `likes("Steve", book("Name", "Author")).`

elaboration1_20.dialogue: I’ve learned a lot of new things... now let’s move on to the task, there’s little time left...
elaboration1_20.speaker: steve

elaboration1_failTask1_01.dialogue: Be more careful, agent! I told you, the tasks are the traps themselves.
elaboration1_failTask1_01.speaker: robot

elaboration2_start.speaker: steve
elaboration2_start.dialogue: Another trap! The door is locked again... We need to enter a code here as well.

elaboration2_01.dialogue: You've already completed 2 tasks! Don't lose heart, sir!
elaboration2_01.speaker: robot

elaboration2_02.dialogue: I think I hear some sounds coming from under this door! It feels like someone is there!
elaboration2_02.speaker: steve

elaboration2_04.dialogue: Me too! But what's even scarier is not completing all the tasks in 6 hours!
elaboration2_04.speaker: steve

elaboration2_05.dialogue: Yes, let's move on to the next task!
elaboration2_05.speaker: robot

elaboration2_06.dialogue: Prolog is a language based on logic. The basic blocks are facts, rules, and queries.

elaboration2_07.dialogue: They allow you to describe knowledge and perform logical inference.

elaboration2_08.dialogue: Simple queries, without any variables, allow for two possible answers: `true` or `false`.

elaboration2_09.dialogue: In the case of a `true` response, it is said that the query succeeded, and the goal was achieved.
elaboration2_09.speaker: steve

elaboration2_10.dialogue: Using variables in queries allows for more complex questions.
elaboration2_10.speaker: steve

elaboration2_11.dialogue:
For example:
`?- likes('Steve','book').` will return `true`.
`?- likes(Who,'book').` will return `Who = 'Steve'`.
elaboration2_11.speaker: steve

elaboration2_12.dialogue: Now let's try to apply the theory to practice.
elaboration2_12.speaker: steve

elaboration2_15.dialogue: You're making progress, agent. It's time to open the room...

elaboration3_start.dialogue: Well, who would have thought that such a cozy study could exist in this house.

elaboration3_01.dialogue: I have the feeling that someone was recently here, even leaving some papers on the desk.

elaboration3_02.dialogue: A very nice and charming room.
elaboration3_02.speaker: robot

elaboration3_03.dialogue: But there is no computer here, so we’ll have to keep searching. Minitnik must have been here just recently.
elaboration3_03.speaker: steve

elaboration3_07.dialogue: Maybe it’s Minitnik decided to return to his office?
elaboration3_07.speaker: steve

elaboration3_08.dialogue: I’ll hide under the table so no one notices me. Ouch, ouch, ouch... another hidden trap here.
elaboration3_08.speaker: steve

elaboration3_09.dialogue: I accidentally triggered some mechanism and ended up in a trap. Metal bars dropped down from all sides...
elaboration3_09.speaker: steve

elaboration3_11.dialogue: You need to complete another task and enter the code. That’s the only way to free yourself.
elaboration3_11.speaker: robot

elaboration3_12.dialogue: Agreed, the bars are too strong... and anyone could come in here! We need to complete the task quickly.
elaboration3_12.speaker: steve

elaboration3_14.dialogue: Let’s review the theory. Oh no! There’s nothing written for the next task...
elaboration3_14.speaker: steve

elaboration3_15.dialogue: Ha, Minitnik is clever, but we won’t be sad. Let’s test our skills.
elaboration3_15.speaker: steve

elaboration3_17.dialogue: Good... Looks like the trap has been deactivated.

elaboration4_start.speaker: steve
elaboration4_start.dialogue: Phew! I made it out! Now I need to hurry and search for the computer!

elaboration4_02.dialogue: Do you hear those strange sounds again? Someone is definitely here!
elaboration4_02.speaker: steve

elaboration4_03.dialogue: It sounds like some kind of mooing. The sounds are coming from that far corner.
elaboration4_03.speaker: robot

elaboration4_04.dialogue: Let’s go check it out! Looks like someone really is there!
elaboration4_04.speaker: steve

elaboration4_05.dialogue: It’s the kidnapped information security specialist, Sarah Parker!
elaboration4_05.speaker: steve

elaboration4_06.dialogue: I’m FBI agent Steve Harrison. Tell me what happened to you...
elaboration4_06.speaker: steve

elaboration4_07.dialogue: Kevin Mitnick kidnapped me last night from my home! He’s gone crazy and needs to be stopped immediately!
elaboration4_07.speaker: sarah

elaboration4_08.dialogue: Please help me get free! I know where the main computer is!

elaboration4_09.dialogue: You’re a brave girl! I’ll complete the task, enter the code, and we’ll free you! Don’t worry!
elaboration4_09.speaker: steve

elaboration4_10.dialogue: I’ll take a look at the tablet, get familiar with the theory...

elaboration4_11.dialogue: Lists are an important structure. Lists allow you to store an arbitrary amount of data.

elaboration4_12.dialogue: A node contains data and a reference (pointer, link) to one or two neighboring nodes.

elaboration4_13.dialogue: Prolog lists are singly linked, with each node containing one reference.

elaboration4_14.dialogue: There are built-in functions to work with lists; let's go over some of them.

elaboration4_15.dialogue: `sum_list(List, Sum)` — calculates the sum of the list elements.

elaboration4_16.dialogue: `member(Elem, List)` — checks if an element exists in the list.

elaboration4_18.dialogue: `length(List, Length)` — calculates the length of the list.

elaboration4_20.dialogue: `delete(InputList, Elem, ResultList)` — removes all elements with a given value from the list, returning a new list.

elaboration4_21.dialogue: Yes, this will be a bit trickier, but we're close to our goal. We can do it!

elaboration5_start.speaker: steve
elaboration5_start.dialogue: Yes! We're almost there! Here’s the computer... though it’s not a supercomputer, it's still a pretty powerful machine!

elaboration5_01.dialogue: Look, the computer is on and loading some files. Should we check what's there?
elaboration5_01.speaker: sarah

elaboration5_02.dialogue: Here’s a whole list of encrypted personal data from the employees of the US Mint. As far as I know, only 10 of them have access to the Fort Knox vault.
elaboration5_02.speaker: steve

elaboration5_03.dialogue: To get inside the vault, each of them must enter their part of the code, and then 'Sim-Sim' will open its doors.
elaboration5_03.speaker: steve

elaboration5_04.dialogue: But this happens extremely rarely. In the entire history of Fort Knox, only three times have outsiders gotten inside.
elaboration5_04.speaker: steve

elaboration5_05.dialogue: Who got that honor? How did they manage to get in?
elaboration5_05.speaker: sarah

elaboration5_06.dialogue: The first person to get in was President Roosevelt in 1943. The second inspection took place only 31 years later.
elaboration5_06.speaker: steve

elaboration5_07.dialogue: The third inspection happened in 2018 because rumors were circulating that there was no gold in the vault.
elaboration5_07.speaker: steve

elaboration5_08.dialogue: However, it turned out to be just rumors, and all the gold was still there.
elaboration5_08.speaker: steve

elaboration5_09.dialogue: I wonder, are the Mint employees also at Mitnick's house, or does he plan to use them secretly?
elaboration5_09.speaker: sarah

elaboration5_10.dialogue: We’ll find out later. For now, we need to stop the virus and enter the code before anyone interrupts us.
elaboration5_10.speaker: steve

elaboration5_12.dialogue: I’ll open the theory now... It’s not there again, but we managed last time.

character(steve).
character(mitnik).```What will the query `character(steve).` return?

character(steve).
